paragraphs.title: Longing for the Beloved and Entrance into the King’s Chambers

answers: The kisses of her beloved’s mouth
easy.explanation: She says, “Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.”
easy.q: What does the woman desire at the beginning of the song?
What does she ask her beloved to do?

easy.explanation: She asks to run after him because the king has brought her into his chambers.
easy.q: Where do they want to run together?

answers: His good ointments and his good name
medium.explanation: His good ointments and name are compared with poured-out ointment, and the virgins love him.
medium.q: What makes the woman want to draw near to her beloved?

medium.explanation: She says, “Thy love is better than wine.”

answers: Vineyard work, searching for a shepherd, and praise of beauty
Longing for the beloved, being drawn to him, and entering the king’s chambers
Jewelry, a feast, and building a house
medium.explanation: The passage moves from longing to being drawn after the beloved and rejoicing with him.
medium.q: What is the main progression in these verses?

answers: The scent causes the ointment to disappear
challenge.explanation: His good ointments and name are presented as reasons why the virgins love him.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the beloved’s ointment and the women’s love?

answers: A desire to draw near and move together
A desire to get away from him
challenge.explanation: The request expresses eagerness for closeness and shared movement.
challenge.q: What does the request “Draw me, we will run after thee” express?

challenge.explanation: The passage focuses on the woman’s love for her beloved and their rejoicing together.
challenge.q: Who are the lovers presented in this passage?

paragraphs.title: The Beautiful Dark Woman and the Search for the Shepherd

easy.explanation: She says, “I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem.”
easy.q: How does the woman describe herself?

easy.explanation: She says, “the sun hath looked upon me.”
easy.q: What caused her skin to become dark?

answers: The shepherd whom her soul loves
easy.explanation: She asks where the one whom her soul loves feeds his flock.

answers: Her mother’s children made her keep them
The shepherd asked her to build a house
medium.explanation: She says, “my mother’s children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards.”
medium.q: Why did the woman have to work in the vineyards?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes her duty to watch over the vineyards.
medium.q: What does “the keeper of the vineyards” mean in context?

answers: Follow the footsteps of the flock
medium.explanation: He tells her to go forth by the footsteps of the flock and feed her kids beside the shepherds’ tents.
medium.q: What does the beloved tell her to do in order to find him?

answers: She is dark in appearance but still beautiful
She is wealthy but without ornaments
She is a shepherdess but does not know sheep
challenge.explanation: She emphasizes that although she is dark, she is still comely.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the woman’s description of herself?

answers: She guarded only her own vineyard
She cared for others’ vineyards and neglected her own
She had never seen a vineyard
challenge.explanation: Her imposed work kept her from caring for her own vineyard.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “mine own vineyard have I not kept”?

answers: She searches in the setting of flocks and shepherds
She searches in a vineyard that is not hers
challenge.explanation: The beloved directs her toward the flock and the shepherds’ tents.
challenge.q: How does the search for the shepherd relate to the woman’s work?

paragraphs.title: Praise of Beauty and Royal Adornment

answers: A company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots
easy.explanation: He says, “I have compared thee ... to a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.”
easy.q: To what does the beloved compare the woman?

answers: Only her work in the vineyards
easy.explanation: He praises her cheeks, neck, jewels, and chains.
easy.q: What does he praise about the woman?

easy.explanation: He says, “We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.”
easy.q: What materials will be used for her ornaments?

answers: It shows that she works in a vineyard
It explains why her skin is dark
medium.explanation: The comparison to Pharaoh’s magnificent horses conveys grandeur and beauty.
medium.q: What does the comparison to Pharaoh’s chariots add to the description?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to jewelry adorning the woman’s cheeks.
medium.q: What are the “rows of jewels” in this passage?

answers: They continue the themes of praise and adornment
They change the subject to fieldwork
They describe the search for the shepherd
medium.explanation: The promised ornaments reinforce the woman’s royal beauty.
medium.q: How do the gold and silver ornaments fit the passage’s overall idea?

answers: A symbolic connection with Israel and the Exodus
Proof that the woman is an Egyptian queen
A description of war among shepherds
challenge.explanation: The reference may be read symbolically in connection with Israel and the Exodus from Egypt.
challenge.q: What possible symbolic association may be suggested by the reference to Pharaoh?

answers: To emphasize his appreciation of her beauty
To command her to guard the vineyards
To keep her away from the palace
challenge.explanation: The promised gold and silver ornaments express admiration and honor.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the promise to make ornaments for her?

answers: From describing the woman to comparing her with royal horses and promising ornaments
From searching for the shepherd to describing punishment
From describing a house to describing vineyards
challenge.explanation: The beloved moves from a grand comparison to praise of her adornment.
challenge.q: What movement of thought occurs in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Perfumes, a Passionate Dream, and Anticipation of Meeting

easy.explanation: The woman says, “my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.”
easy.q: What fragrance is mentioned at the king’s table?

easy.explanation: She says, “A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved unto me.”
easy.q: To what is the beloved compared when he is close to the woman?

easy.explanation: He is compared to “a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En-gedi.”
easy.q: To what is the beloved compared in the vineyards of En-gedi?

answers: They belong to fragrant imagery surrounding the beloved
They describe the work of the woman’s brothers
medium.explanation: The passage uses fragrant plants and substances to portray the beloved and anticipation of him.
medium.q: What do spikenard, myrrh, and camphire have in common in these verses?

medium.explanation: Spikenard is presented as a fragrant substance whose scent fills the setting.
medium.q: What is spikenard in this context?

answers: The beloved is imagined as very near to her heart
The beloved is far away from her
The woman is describing vineyard labor
medium.explanation: The image expresses intimate emotional nearness.
medium.q: What can be understood from the myrrh being “betwixt my breasts”?

answers: A possible place where the woman expects to meet her beloved
A memory of her brothers’ work
A sign that the house has already been built
challenge.explanation: The image of En-gedi can suggest a setting connected with expectation of meeting him.
challenge.q: What may the cluster of camphire in En-gedi represent in the passage?

answers: The beloved is pictured through fragrant images while the woman anticipates him
The woman describes only practical work
The beloved offers only literal jewelry
challenge.explanation: The fragrant images create a dreamlike portrait of a beloved whose presence is awaited.
challenge.q: How does the passage combine imagination and expectation?

answers: The bundle of myrrh held near the heart
The distance from the shepherds’ tents
The work in the family vineyards
challenge.explanation: The myrrh lying close to her expresses powerful nearness to the beloved.
challenge.q: What most strengthens the sense of closeness in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Mutual Love and the Dream of a Shared Home

answers: That she is beautiful only because of her ornaments
easy.explanation: He says, “Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair.”
easy.q: What does the beloved say about the woman’s beauty?

easy.explanation: The beloved says, “thou hast doves’ eyes.”
easy.q: What are the woman’s eyes compared to?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “The beams of our house are cedar.”
easy.q: What are the beams of the house made of?

answers: She says that he also is fair and pleasant
She asks him to leave the vineyard
medium.explanation: She replies, “Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant.”
medium.q: How does the woman respond to the beloved’s praise?

medium.explanation: The green bed suggests freshness, vitality, and pleasantness.
medium.q: What does “green” suggest about their bed?

answers: Mutual praise leads to an imagined shared and pleasant place
The praise leads to vineyard labor
The praise leads to separation from the beloved
medium.explanation: The exchange of praise culminates in a vision of a shared home.
medium.q: How does the passage develop from praise of beauty to the image of a house?

challenge.explanation: Each lover praises the beauty and pleasantness of the other.
challenge.q: What does the mutual praise of the two lovers express?

answers: Love rooted in a stable and peaceful home
challenge.explanation: The house imagery suggests stability, rootedness, and peace.
challenge.q: What may the cedar beams and fir rafters symbolize?

answers: Love moves from longing toward a vision of a shared home
Love ends with the search for the shepherd
Love focuses only on golden ornaments
challenge.explanation: The ending presents a vision of freshness, stability, home, and mutual affection.
challenge.q: What idea best summarizes the end of the passage?

short_answers.question: According to verse 2, what is better than wine?
short_answers.explanation: The woman says, “thy love is better than wine.”

short_answers.question: According to verse 6, what has the woman not kept?
short_answers.explanation: She says, “mine own vineyard have I not kept.”

short_answers.question: According to verse 17, what are the rafters of their house made of?
short_answers.explanation: The verse says, “our rafters of fir.”
